title: Projective logarithmic resolution over an excellent affine base
statement: Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], put $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $(V,M)$ be an integral fs log regular scheme, quasi-projective of finite type over $B$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. There exists a finite tower of saturated log blowups $b:(Y,M_Y)\to(V,M)$ whose underlying composite is projective and birational, with $Y$ integral and regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The log morphism $b$ is log etale [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. For any locally Noetherian fs log scheme $D$ and any log-smooth morphism $(V,M)\to D$, the composite $(Y,M_Y)\to D$ is log smooth. Birational means inducing an isomorphism between dense opens; length-zero towers are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.4.6(i), 3.4.8--Theorem 3.4.9, pp.111--112; VI 1.7--1.8, p.70; XVI 3.7, p.254. Finite normalized blowup towers are projective here; the quasi-projective affine-base hypothesis gives the finite-projective-space convention.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7, final geometric step: logarithmic blowup of X double-prime/H with regular total space.
